hook.text: Can you build a cell from non-living components? Protocells try — lipid vesicles with encapsulated reactions.

buildup.text: Fatty acid vesicles form spontaneously in water — trapping enzymes and nucleic acids inside a membrane boundary.

discovery.text: Protocells can grow by incorporating new fatty acids — and divide when they reach a critical size.

twist.text: No protocell replicates its internal information yet — coupling genome replication to vesicle division remains unsolved.

climax.text: Protocell research bridges synthetic biology and origin-of-life science — building life bottom-up to understand how it began.

punchline.text: Assemble life from parts — protocells explore the boundary between chemistry and biology.

quiz.question: What is the key unsolved problem in protocell research?
options: Protocells cannot form membranes from simple molecules
Coupling genome replication to vesicle division has not been achieved
Protocells dissolve within minutes of forming

details.summary: Protocells are artificial cell-like structures assembled from synthetic components including lipid vesicles, simple genetic circuits, and minimal metabolic systems. They aim to create the simplest possible system that exhibits life-like properties such as self-replication and metabolism.
details.whyItMatters: Protocell research addresses the fundamental question of how life can arise from non-living chemistry. Understanding minimal life requirements informs both origin-of-life science and the design of artificial living systems for biotechnology
takeaways: Protocells are synthetic structures that mimic basic cellular properties
Lipid vesicles provide compartmentalization similar to biological membranes
Research explores the minimum requirements for life-like behavior

faq.question: What components are needed to build a protocell?
faq.answer: A membrane boundary typically made from lipid vesicles, an information system like RNA or DNA, and an energy source driving metabolism. Current protocells achieve some but not all life-like properties simultaneously. Self-replicating protocells remain an unsolved grand challenge.

faq.question: How do protocells differ from naturally derived minimal cells?
faq.answer: Minimal cells like JCVI-syn3.0 are stripped-down versions of natural organisms. Protocells are built bottom-up from non-living components. Minimal cells are alive and self-replicating; protocells mimic some properties of life but have not yet achieved autonomous replication.
